title: RAW UNREVIEWED: attainability of the27-entry prefix-code lower bound by three fixed head-pair constructions
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, no result. For each of the three GDT1234 unforced heads cfh,cph,q, keep the other21 working signs as singleton entries and give the chosen head one two-unit code with each of the22 possible followers. Test complete coverage of unchanged1233whole groups, remove unused entries only after full coverage, and compare the actually used nontrivial table size with the established27-entry lower bound. This is a fixed three-construction upper-bound question, not a historical alphabet, semantic writer, new source, repaired22-entry model or unrestricted codebook optimizer.

design.authorship: Root proposed this cost-tightness question after declining the unjustified<=26general-UD solver. Bounded producer checked primary predecessors and the mathematical contract without target payloads or outcomes.
design.question: Is GDT1234's lower bound27 attained by a complete actually used prefix-free table on each unchanged reader-specific1233word panel?

input_contract.alphabet: Exactly the22 indivisible working-unit labels of1233/1234. Multiletter ASCII labels such as cfh are one unit, never characters to split.
input_contract.population: All unchanged complete eligible groups in1233GROUPS, with each reading assessed separately. This is the existing scoped panel, not every manuscript group or a newly selected source.
input_contract.preserved: Exact working-unit sequences and whole-word boundaries, including rare forms; no error allowance, source-letter values, language or word meanings.

full_construction.offered_table: For chosen g, C_g=(A\{g}) union {g h : h in A}. There are21singleton entries and22two-unit entries,43offered entries in total.
full_construction.reading: Scan each whole group left to right. A unit unequal to g is one code. A unit g consumes itself and exactly the next working unit as one code, including the pair gg. Do not apply the head rule recursively to the consumed second unit. A final unpaired g makes that entire group unparseable.
full_construction.uniqueness: All singleton heads differ from g; all g-headed entries have equal length2. Therefore C_g is prefix-free and its greedy parse is unique.
full_construction.writing: An abstract source symbol assigned to a used singleton is written as that unit; an abstract symbol assigned to a used pair is written as that pair. A learned symbol-to-entry table would still be required for a meaningful source; this proposal assigns none.
full_construction.pruning: Only after all retained groups parse, discard entries never used in those complete parses. The remaining table is still prefix-free and covers the same panel. No deletion of a used entry or failed group is allowed.
full_construction.nontriviality: At least one two-unit entry must actually occur in a successful whole-group parse. An unused offered compound is not evidence of a nontrivial code.
full_construction.human_cost: One special-head recognition rule plus the explicit retained source-symbol table, if later given. Mathematical attainability alone does not pay language, vocabulary or semantic binding.

decisions.complete_size27: Full coverage plus actual compound use plus exactly27used entries supplies an upper bound27. Together with the unchanged1234lower bound, this certifies exact minimum27 for the stipulated nontrivial prefix-free class on that reader's panel.
decisions.complete_size_above27: Preserve the complete explicit table as an upper-bound witness. This does not attain27 and is not a failed coverage construction. Compare with the already published larger prefix bases without claiming historical plausibility.
decisions.complete_size_below27: Treat as a contradiction of validation, units, population or premises requiring diagnosis; never silently announce an improved bound.
decisions.incomplete_coverage: The specified two-unit-head construction fails on exactly the retained unparseable whole groups. It does not show that all prefix tables of size27fail.
decisions.zero_compound_use: Identity-only coverage is not a nontrivial upper-bound witness.
decisions.stop: No code length3, additional special heads, follower pruning of observed pairs, table search, source alphabet assignment, new corpus, alias or error-budget follow-up.

design.q_prior_limit: GDT1234 REPORT already gives the q-headed nontrivial lower bound32forIT/ZL and33forRF. Accordingly q cannot attain27 under unchanged premises; retain it only as the predeclared comparison construction, not a fresh chance of a27positive.
design.activity_limit: Report how often the compound rule actually affects complete groups and how many compound entries are used. An exact minimum may be attained through rare forms while almost all writing stays singleton. Neither full coverage nor optimal table count explains common repeated parts, q/o frequency, semantics or a full statistical profile.

known_predecessors.scope: Lower bound27;19forced singleton signs; onlycfh/cph/qcanheadlongcodes; qbound32/33. Existing complete prefix bases have104IT/83RF/82ZL entries and are explicitly not minimum-size tables. No27/28table was constructed.
Rare-support dependence of the27bound is retained. Do not drop low-support groups to obtain attainment.

Examined one compound entry plus21singletons, exactly22entries, with exception/activity costs. The present finite offered table contains every follower pair for one fixed head and asks exact coverage/upper-bound attainment, not an exception-budget repair of that old family.
General freeUD is broader; the prefix-only27minimum must not be exported to it. No generalUDsolver is selected by this proposal.
Fixed<=22table exclusion remains. Present question is explicit tightness of an already proved larger lower bound, not claiming that a bigger alphabet is more historically plausible.
